name: Messina router hop() recursive VAA re-emission (Opulous OPUL)
summary: The Messina router on Avalanche, the Wormhole emitter every destination bridge trusts, re-publishes any verified VAA through hop() without checking its emitter or target chain. Attackers fed the router's own output VAAs back into hop(), turning single deposits into many claimable VAAs that released escrowed tokens on Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base and Polygon.

notes: Loss is gross escrow depletion (loss.mjs over every listed redemption, victims the Messina escrows), not net of the attackers' seed deposits (rule 11). PEPE2.0 and PEIPEI were never sold and are omitted.

OPUL, dumped with large price impact, and BOBO are valued at realised DEX proceeds net of attacker purchases (rule 12), taken from the prior review's reconstruction; OPUL moved to exchanges or kept, about 80M, is not valued, so the figure is a lower bound.

Redemptions were found through each spoke's Etherscan txlist (direct calls only) and hub hops through the hub txlist up to block 96965864; hop() was never disabled, so later or relayed redemptions are not covered.
